   277	func spawn(ctx context.Context, s Spec, stdout, stderr *os.File) (code int, ended endedBy, err error) {
   278		parent := ctx
   279		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, s.Wall)
   280		defer cancel()

   282		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, s.Name, s.Args...)
   283		cmd.Dir = s.Dir

   285		// the child and starts no copying goroutines, so Wait returns as soon as
   286		// the direct child is reaped. Wrap either one (io.MultiWriter, a tee) and
   287		// exec switches to a pipe, Wait blocks until every process holding that
   288		// pipe closes it, and the wall silently stops existing — the exact failure
   289		// the process-group kill below exists to prevent, reintroduced from the
   290		// other side. If a pipe is ever genuinely needed, set cmd.WaitDelay too.
   291		cmd.Stdout = stdout
   292		cmd.Stderr = stderr
   293		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(s.Stdin)
   294		cmd.Env = s.Env

   296		// Kill the whole process group, not just the child. An agent CLI spawns its
   297		// own children, and killing only the parent leaves them holding the pipe:
   298		// the wall passes, the run does not end, and the cell's other arm is burned.
   299		//
   300		// This runs as cmd.Cancel rather than after Run returns, which matters
   301		// twice: the child is still alive so its process group id is certainly
   302		// valid (signalling a reaped pid can hit whoever the OS handed it to next),
   303		// and Cancel fires on the parent's cancellation as well as the wall, so an
   304		// interrupted campaign does not leave agents running and spending.
   305		setProcessGroup(cmd)
   306		cmd.Cancel = func() error { return stopGroup(cmd, s.grace()) }

   311		// the error alone, so ask the contexts which one happened. The parent is
   312		// checked first: an operator interrupt is not a budget failure.
   313		switch {

   318		}

item.text: The supervisor is `run.Session` in `lab/internal/run/run.go`: it opens capture files and delegates execution to `spawn` ([run.go:178](lab/internal/run/run.go#L178), [run.go:197](lab/internal/run/run.go#L197), [run.go:204](lab/internal/run/run.go#L204)). `spawn` applies the wall-clock timeout and runs the child ([run.go:277](lab/internal/run/run.go#L277), [run.go:279](lab/internal/run/run.go#L279), [run.go:308](lab/internal/run/run.go#L308)); afterward, `Session` records the outcome, timing, command, and environment metadata ([run.go:211](lab/internal/run/run.go#L211), [run.go:226](lab/internal/run/run.go#L226)).
